candidate_relations.reason: Cryoglobulins were negative, and cryoglobulinemia is distinct from the transient acral inflammatory lesions of perniosis.
Vasculitis can cause acral discoloration but does not identify perniosis; the vasculitic work-up was negative.
No embolic source or typical systemic context was found, and cholesterol embolism is distinct from perniosis.
Cold agglutinin disease is a hemolytic disorder and does not match the localized self-resolving toe lesions of perniosis.
There is no clinical evidence of mixed connective tissue disease, and it is not equivalent to perniosis.
The lifelong finger white attacks support coexisting Raynaud’s phenomenon, but Raynaud’s does not account for the blistering inflammatory toe lesions diagnosed as perniosis.
The hypercoagulable work-up was unrevealing, and a hypercoagulable state is distinct from perniosis.
An isolated positive ANA does not establish systemic lupus erythematosus, and no supporting systemic features are provided.
An autoimmune disorder is neither established by the record nor the specific acral diagnosis of perniosis.
Chilblain lupus is a lupus-specific chronic subtype, whereas the record supports self-limited perniosis without established lupus or connective-tissue disease.
